why: The behavior-mode layer already ships — 68 modes, six behavior dimensions, a GML affinity graph, and a MathML policy declaring four weight classes and a bounded learning delta — but nothing gated it. Two hazards follow. First, the safeguards live only in prose annotations, so a caller could treat an affinity as a probability, a bias as a gradient, or a verified execution as helpfulness. Second, the repository now states **two different** W_effective laws, and conflating them would be a silent correctness error.

name_collision.mml_here: MathML — `data/grammar/mml/v1/` holds 43 MathML content dictionaries, one per daemon, with `csymbol cd="urn:kuhul:daemon-*:v1"` symbols
name_collision.proposed: Micronaut Mode Markup, as a separate markup for mode configuration and learning policy
name_collision.decision: the established MML is MathML and is kept; mode configuration lives in the JSON + MathML policy pair above. A new markup would need its own extension (e.g. `M3`), not the name MML, because `*.mml` already means MathML content dictionaries here

weight_classes.law: the four weights are distinct feature sources, never one number, and none of them is a gradient
weight_classes.combination: the MathML policy states W_effective as a sum of the four terms and requires that a runtime define normalization and combination before summing them; a sum without declared normalization is a typed refusal

two_effective_laws.law: this repository states two W_effective formulas for two different things, and they must not be conflated

behavior_modes.meaning: additive composition of four distinct feature sources

asx_corpus_gate.meaning: a multiplicative gate: a frozen corpus prior scaled by a learned weight

two_effective_laws.rule: one is a sum of feature sources, the other is a product of a prior and a learned scale; a value computed under one must never be reported as the other

mode_selection.law: selection ranks modes by preference; it never renormalises a preference into a probability, never invents a mode that is not in the catalog, and never writes W_learned

learning_update.not_a_gradient: this is not a differentiable gradient; calling it one would require a declared differentiable objective, which the contract does not have

safeguards.provenance: verified_reward needs its own provenance and must never be inferred merely from response verification
safeguards.bounded: the update is clipped to explicit bounds; an unbounded update is refused
safeguards.validated_and_authorized: a persistent update requires Ch'en validation and Xul authorization in addition to user/app policy
safeguards.separate_from_patterns: the learning layer never rewrites the pattern/grammar layer, so behaviour evolves without silently editing the templates

graph.subject: data/daemon_behavior_modes.gml
graph.declared_comment: edge weights are affinities, not probabilities or learned gradients, and XCFE decides whether a requested mode combination is admissible
graph.coverage: the shipped graph declares `id 68` but carries only 12 nodes and 9 edges, so it is an illustrative partial graph over the 68-mode catalog rather than a complete one; the gate checks the shipped set exactly so a silently truncated graph is caught

invariants.BM1: the catalog keeps 68 modes across the seven categories, each mode declares all six behavior dimensions with values from the declared dimension vocabularies, and an unknown dimension value is refused
invariants.BM2: the four weight classes stay distinct; none is reported as a gradient, and an affinity is never reported as a probability
invariants.BM3: W_learned is never written by mode selection, and the learning layer never rewrites the pattern layer
invariants.BM4: a bounded learning delta is clipped to explicit bounds; an unbounded or out-of-bounds update is refused rather than clamped silently
invariants.BM5: verified_reward requires its own provenance; a reward inferred from response verification alone is refused
invariants.BM6: a persistent update requires Ch'en validation and Xul authorization as well as policy; without them nothing is written
invariants.BM7: selection honours an explicit override, ranks a primary plus weighted secondaries without renormalising preferences into probabilities, and asks (or takes the neutral default) for an unknown mode instead of inventing one
invariants.BM8: the two W_effective laws are kept apart: the additive four-source composition requires declared normalization, and neither may be reported as the other
invariants.BM9: the therapy boundary holds: non-clinical support only, no diagnosis or treatment claims, crisis routed to the host safety policy, and persistent memory only on explicit opt-in
invariants.BM10: the graph's edge weights are affinities within (0, 1) using only the four declared relations, and admissibility of a combination remains XCFE's decision
invariants.BM11: every mode carries a unique pictogram in the declared form, and a pictogram never collides with an ASX unit glyph
invariants.BM12: eight behavior dimensions are declared; memory and autonomy are among them, and both ship at their least-authority value with any raise being an explicit act
invariants.BM13: every mode belongs to exactly one class (personality, task, metacognitive) derived from its category by the declared mapping, and the class carries no authority
invariants.BM14: every mode's bias vector carries a provenance tag marking it an illustrative prior; a bias tagged as a learned weight is refused

dimensions.law: eight dimensions, not one personality per mode: buddy + scientist + skeptic compose a research partner without a new personality bank

mode_classes.law: each mode belongs to exactly one class; the class is a routing aid and carries no authority

pictograms.rule: glyph = U+27C1 followed by the mode id uppercased with hyphens replaced by underscores
pictograms.law: every mode carries exactly one pictogram, pictograms are unique, and none may equal an ASX unit glyph

least_authority_defaults.law: memory and autonomy default to the least authority that still works; raising either is an explicit per-mode act, never inferred from a mode's name or description
